# TASK-241: Persist observations and reconcile current file state safely

## Goal

Implement the durable identity and reconciliation core that can answer what is present now without confusing missing coverage, scope changes, renames, replacements, or restarts with deletion.

## Deliverables

- Versioned evidence-state schema and migration
- Atomic observation reconciler
- Materialized current-file projection
- Coverage-gap and restart handling
- State-machine test suite

## Allowed Write Scope

- Sources/DiskStewardCore/EvidenceStore/**
- Sources/DiskStewardCore/Monitoring/**

- Tests/DiskStewardCoreTests/Monitoring/**
- Tests/DiskStewardAppTests/EvidenceState/**
- docs/tasks/evidence/TASK-241/**

## Non-Goals

- Guessing exact deletion time
- Treating path as permanent identity
- Deleting user files
- Silently discarding partial-scan evidence

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AC-241-01` — Database migrations persist scope versions, observation runs and per-root completeness, stable file identity when available, temporal path bindings, state observations, current state, change events, and coverage gaps without discarding existing evidence.
- `AC-241-02` — One transaction commits an observation, its derived events, path-binding changes, current-state changes, and coverage result; retries are idempotent and recovery cannot expose half-applied observations.
- `AC-241-03` — Complete same-scope observations reconcile baseline, create, modify, truncate, rename, replace, delete, and path reuse, while partial or unavailable roots produce unknown or stale state and scope removal produces out-of-scope state.
- `AC-241-04` — Restart loads the last committed state and records offline or unreconciled coverage intervals; it never treats the first post-restart scan as proof that all intervening changes occurred at startup.
- `AC-241-05` — The normative A/B/C scenario returns only A and C as current after a complete deletion scan, retains B as a tombstoned historical object, and never emits B deleted after a partial scan.

## Required Evidence

- `EVREQ-241-01` (state-reconciliation-test) — Migration, transaction-failure, retry, restart, complete and partial coverage, scope change, A/B/C deletion, rename, replace, path reuse, hard-link or clone disclosure, and current-projection consistency fixtures.
